brand.name: SUPERAGENT
brand.one_liner: AI agents for insurance call handling, follow-up, producer training, retention and quoting.

pages.excerpt: The homepage offers six agents for insurance agencies and a 14-day trial. Product examples span call capture, follow-up and producer coaching.

Lead lists, new form submissions and dormant accounts feed multi-touch campaigns across phone, SMS and email. Qualified replies are handed to producers. This supports a follow-through campaign direction.

Monthly plans: restricted Starter $299; Pro $499; Scale $999; Enterprise from $2,499. Pro includes 1,350 inbound/outbound minutes and 1,050 quotes. Starter applicants need approval; overage packs are extra.
The agent qualifies calls, routes service/claims/billing/sales requests, books appointments and provides a contextual human handoff. The FAQ lists Starter at $249, inconsistent with the pricing page.
Listed connections include Applied Epic, EZLynx, HawkSoft, QQCatalyst and AMS360. The page describes call logging, CRM contact creation, appointment booking and follow-up email workflows.

nodes.text: Insurance AI agents for inbound, outbound, training, live calls, retention and quoting
Qualify inbound calls, book appointments, and hand context to a human producer
Work new and dormant leads through phone, SMS, email and voicemail sequences
Independent and captive US insurance agencies
Plans cover individual producers, small teams and enterprise agencies
Missed overflow calls and incomplete lead follow-up
Producers spend time on routine dialing and document collection
14-day free trial on the homepage; personalized product demo
Insurance workflows spanning reception, outbound follow-up and producer development
Connections to AMS, CRM, telephony and calendar tools
Test clear agency workflow demonstrations with specific handoff details

missing: Resolve the Starter price discrepancy between pricing and inbound FAQ.
Private competitor spend and conversion data are unavailable.

insights.title: Insurance reception is already contested
insights.observation: Sonant explicitly targets P&C agencies in Meta copy and insurance claims in Google search. Its website also promises agency-system updates and human escalation. Insurance specialization alone is shared positioning.
insights.recommendation: Show the complete workflow: capture intent, add the agency context, and hand off to the producer. Compare the actual workflow rather than claiming nobody serves insurance.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

insights.title: The missed paid lead is not an untouched angle
insights.observation: Smith.ai Meta ads describe marketing money wasted when calls go unanswered. SUPERAGENT already runs a missed-call video alongside outbound-agent image creative.
insights.recommendation: Test an original inbound-to-follow-up demonstration against the existing missed-call message. Judge the test on qualified appointments, not how common the hook is.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

insights.title: Workflow breadth is a stronger test than another receptionist slogan
insights.observation: SUPERAGENT’s Google image ad promotes outbound automation; its product pages connect old lead lists, new inquiries and multiple follow-up channels. Frontdesk also sells a broader customer platform.
insights.recommendation: Test a specific insurance workflow such as quote follow-up with a producer handoff. Demonstrate it; do not present platform breadth as exclusive.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

insights.title: Human reassurance is part of the competition
insights.observation: AnswerConnect uses a named receptionist and human-service imagery in Google ads. Smith.ai promotes AI reception with live-agent help. These creatives directly address trust and handoff.
insights.recommendation: Show a real call example and the moment a person takes over. Test caller confidence separately from time-saving claims.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

insights.title: Advertised entry prices hide different jobs and units
insights.observation: PATLive’s $49 entry plan includes no minutes; Goodcall bills by distinct monthly callers. Rosie’s $49 tier sends scheduling links, while direct calendar booking starts at $149.
insights.recommendation: Compare a fixed call workload and required features before writing savings copy. A low base price is not a comparable cost per booked appointment.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

insights.title: Resolve Superagent’s price mismatch before advertising it
insights.observation: SUPERAGENT’s pricing page lists restricted Starter at $299/month, while its inbound FAQ still says $249/month. The main Pro plan is $499.
insights.recommendation: Use the verified trial or a demo CTA for now. Reconcile the public pricing pages before sending paid traffic to a price-specific promise.
insights.limitation: Two public pages disagree at the time of capture; the correct checkout charge was not independently confirmed.

insights.title: Comparison content is an observed acquisition tactic
insights.observation: Synthflow has a Google creative explicitly offering a Retell review. The offer captures buyers comparing features and price rather than only broad AI-receptionist demand.
insights.recommendation: Build a factual Superagent-versus-Sonant workflow comparison with current feature and pricing sources. Treat paid promotion as a test, not a proven winner.
insights.limitation: Interpretation of observed messaging; no spend, CTR or conversion performance was obtained.

evidence.subject: Synthflow
evidence.title: AgentFlow AI GmbH — Google creative CR10933541917207560193

insights.title: Repeated ad IDs are not independent winning ideas
insights.observation: All eight captured Sonant Meta records use the same hiring-oriented headline and core body. Two were listed active; one began July 8. Variations and historical records inflate the apparent number of ideas.
insights.recommendation: Group creatives by message before planning tests. Use repetition and observed age to identify messaging worth studying, without inferring conversion performance.
insights.limitation: A point-in-time library sample does not show uninterrupted delivery, spend or ad-level outcomes.

insights.title: ChatGPT cannot be treated as an empty channel
insights.observation: An independent ad-capture service records two Smith.ai placements in ChatGPT. These are third-party observations, not an official advertiser or delivery feed.
insights.recommendation: Remove the no-competitors claim. Treat ChatGPT as an unmeasured test channel and evaluate your own campaign results.
insights.limitation: Independent captures were observed; current delivery, targeting and completeness cannot be established.

concepts.name: Your team is constantly interrupted
concepts.angle: Make the cost of a missed call immediate
concepts.why: Buyer research highlights missed calls and coverage outside office hours. The reused competitor layout is redrawn in official Superagent black and lime so the interruption cost is immediate, while the copy connects it to giving producers selling time back.
concepts.headline: Your team is constantly interrupted
concepts.body: SUPERAGENT gives producers their selling time back.
concepts.visual: A minimal vertical Superagent text ad: official wordmark at the top, centered dark copy, and constantly interrupted highlighted in brand lime #BFD300 on a light grey field.

concepts.name: Don’t let your warm leads go cold.
concepts.angle: Create urgency around leads that need follow-up
concepts.why: The collected outbound research emphasizes working existing and dormant leads through calls, texts, and email. The copy frames delayed follow-up as a missed opportunity and gives insurance agencies a concrete reason to explore Superagent. The familiar office scene and prominent brand mark keep the product recognizable.
concepts.headline: Don’t let your warm leads go cold.
concepts.body: SUPERAGENT follows up by call, text, and email to help your insurance agency stay in the running.
concepts.visual: The original insurance-office scene with a phone and SUPERAGENT logo card. Use clear brand and product copy without invented customer scenarios.
